question.problem: The eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 3k+1 & 3\end{aligned}]$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-k$ is  $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$ Determine the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that the eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =\lambda v \\ [\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 3k+1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] & =-k[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3k+16\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-k \\ -5k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2=-k, \\ 3k+16=-5k\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for $k$ in the first equation, we get

$$
2=-k\,⟹\,k=-2.
$$

Now, substituting $k=-2$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3k+16 & =-5k \\ 3\cdot (-2)+16 & =-5\cdot (-2) \\ 10 & =10,\end{aligned}
$$

which is a true statement.

Therefore, the solution of the system is $k=-2.$
